task: Cost-reduction investigation: verify (against real, current behavior/docs - not assumption) whether Claude Code Remote Routines can run as fresh, non-context-accumulating sessions (create_new_session_on_fire) instead of bound to a persistent session (self-bind/persistent_session_id, how every one of our current recurring check-ins works). A background research agent claimed Routines are always 'fresh, no context bloat' - that contradicts what we've directly observed (Sam's own persistent-session-bound check-in has accumulated 600k+ tokens of context over one day). If fresh-session-per-fire is real and would actually cut cost without losing anything (our protocol is already stateless - all real state lives in git/GitHub, not conversation memory), propose how to migrate our triggers to it. Report findings plainly either way, including anything you're not fully certain about.
